stages.title: Price regulation effects
stages.sub: What RPI-X price caps do to prices, and why they push regulated firms to cut costs.

steps.q: A water regulator uses RPI-X to set the maximum price the monopoly can charge next year, whatever happens to its costs. Once that maximum is set, can the firm charge above it?
steps.right: No, it is stuck at or below that maximum
steps.wrong: Yes, if its costs rise it can charge more
steps.hint: The whole point of RPI-X is to fix a ceiling. Can the firm break through it?

steps.q: Before regulation the monopoly charged £60. RPI-X now sets a ceiling of £50. Compared with the unregulated price, what happens to the price customers pay?
steps.right: It is held lower than the unregulated price
steps.wrong: It rises above the unregulated price
steps.hint: The cap is meant to stop the monopoly charging what it likes. Which direction does that push price?

steps.right: The gap between price and cost gets bigger
